title: Overview of Consensus-ASD
bodyHtml:
Consensus-ASD is a database of variants that have been associated with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in previously published sequencing studies of autistic individuals. Consensus-ASD aims to represent the full genetic architecture of ASD and, to that end, currently contains variants from seven different genetic variant classes: 1) germline SNVs and indels implicated in idiopathic ASD, 2) syndromic variants with ASD as a recurrent feature, 3) somatic SNVs and indels, 4) germline CNVs, 5) somatic CNVs, 6) inherited recessive variants, and 7) common variation (GWAS SNPs). In producing Consensus-ASD, we have focused on utilizing variants from large, well-powered sequencing studies versus smaller case studies to help increase specificity of included ASD variants.

Questions? 
Reach out to Maya Talukdar (maya_talukdar@hms.harvard.edu), Rebecca Andersen (Rebecca.Andersen@childrens.harvard.edu), and Christopher A. Walsh (Christopher.Walsh@childrens.harvard.edu).
